title: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb
body:
Read the chapter → [Exodus 32](/bible/exodus/32)

**[Exodus 32:1-6](/bible/exodus/32#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/exodus/32#v1)</sup> And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/exodus/32#v2)</sup> And Aaron said unto them, Break off the golden earrings, which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters, and bring them unto me.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/exodus/32#v3)</sup> And all the people brake off the golden earrings which were in their ears, and brought them unto Aaron.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/exodus/32#v4)</sup> And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/exodus/32#v5)</sup> And when Aaron saw it, he built an altar before it; and Aaron made proclamation, and said, To morrow is a feast to the Lord.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/exodus/32#v6)</sup> And they rose up early on the morrow, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.

- When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, they gathered unto Aaron: Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, we wot not what is become of him. Any time deliverance did not come when Israel wanted it, the nation rebelled, and Moses and the leadership got the blame; the same spirit is against the leadership of Israel to this day.
- Aaron said break off the golden earrings which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters. Men and women both wore earrings in the scriptures, and it is not sin.
- Aaron received the gold, fashioned it with a graving tool, and made a molten calf, and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt. Aaron saw the miracles in Egypt and was set up as high priest, yet he succumbed to the pressure of the people; that is why the Lord chose Moses specifically to lead, because Moses could not be moved by any means.
- Aaron built an altar before it and made proclamation, To morrow is a feast to the LORD; and the people rose up early, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play. Israel kept provoking God, and the Lord still brought the nation into the promised land as he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

  Precepts:
  - **[1 Corinthians 10:1-7](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v1)</sup> Moreover, brethren, I would not that ye should be ignorant, how that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea;
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v2)</sup> And were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea;
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v3)</sup> And did all eat the same spiritual meat;
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v4)</sup> And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v5)</sup> But with many of them God was not well pleased: for they were overthrown in the wilderness.
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v6)</sup> Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v7)</sup> Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.

    All our fathers were under the cloud and were baptized unto Moses, and that Rock was Christ; the Corinthians were Israelites. Neither be ye idolaters, as it is written, the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.

**[Exodus 32:7-10](/bible/exodus/32#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/exodus/32#v7)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves:
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/exodus/32#v8)</sup> They have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them: they have made them a molten calf, and have worshipped it, and have sacrificed thereunto, and said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which have brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/exodus/32#v9)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people:
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/exodus/32#v10)</sup> Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation.

- The Lord told Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. They turned aside quickly out of the way, made a molten calf, worshipped it, and sacrificed thereunto. Not forty days gone, and they had already left his commandments.
- The spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left. It is the same coming into this truth: the evil carried in from the world will corrupt you and turn you from the Lord if it is not put off.
- I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people. That has been Israel's reputation with the Father from the beginning; without the laws of God we are a carnal, rebellious people, which is why these last days call for humbleness and repentance, not bringing the world's rhetoric into the congregation.
- Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation. Moses was of the tribe of Levi, of the seed of Jacob, so the Lord could have started over with him.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ecclesiastes 5:1](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/ecclesiastes/5#v1)</sup> Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.

    Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God; the evil still in a man from the world will corrupt him as it did our forefathers.

**[Exodus 32:11-14](/bible/exodus/32#v11)**

> <sup>[11](/bible/exodus/32#v11)</sup> And Moses besought the Lord his God, and said, Lord, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand?
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/exodus/32#v12)</sup> Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains, and to consume them from the face of the earth? Turn from thy fierce wrath, and repent of this evil against thy people.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/exodus/32#v13)</sup> Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, thy servants, to whom thou swarest by thine own self, and saidst unto them, I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and all this land that I have spoken of will I give unto your seed, and they shall inherit it for ever.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/exodus/32#v14)</sup> And the Lord repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people.

- Moses besought the LORD his God: LORD, why doth thy wrath wax hot against thy people, which thou hast brought forth out of the land of Egypt with great power, and with a mighty hand? Moses had compassion and stood in the middle, interceding and mediating between the people and God.
- Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains? And remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom thou swarest by thine own self to multiply their seed as the stars of heaven, and to give the land to their seed for ever.
- And the LORD repented of the evil which he thought to do unto his people. The Most High does not repent as a man; he has no one to answer to, he simply turned from the anger of that moment. He was never going to break his covenant, for consuming the people would have destroyed all the seed of Jacob except Moses; Moses was there to remind him of his own word.
- From the questions: the Lord dealt with Moses on a level where Moses could speak to him so, but the outcome stood on what was declared from the beginning; had it been his pleasure to destroy, nothing Moses said could have stayed it.

  Precepts:
  - **[Isaiah 46:10](/bible/isaiah/46#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/isaiah/46#v10)</sup> Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure:

    Declaring the end from the beginning; my counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure.

**[Exodus 32:15-20](/bible/exodus/32#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/exodus/32#v15)</sup> And Moses turned, and went down from the mount, and the two tables of the testimony were in his hand: the tables were written on both their sides; on the one side and on the other were they written.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/exodus/32#v16)</sup> And the tables were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, graven upon the tables.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/exodus/32#v17)</sup> And when Joshua heard the noise of the people as they shouted, he said unto Moses, There is a noise of war in the camp.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/exodus/32#v18)</sup> And he said, It is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither is it the voice of them that cry for being overcome: but the noise of them that sing do I hear.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/exodus/32#v19)</sup> And it came to pass, as soon as he came nigh unto the camp, that he saw the calf, and the dancing: and Moses’ anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/exodus/32#v20)</sup> And he took the calf which they had made, and burnt it in the fire, and ground it to powder, and strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it.

- Moses went down from the mount with the two tables of the testimony in his hand, written on both their sides; the tables were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, graven upon the tables.
- Joshua heard the noise of the people and said, There is a noise of war in the camp; Moses answered, It is not the voice of them that shout for mastery, neither the voice of them that cry for being overcome, but the noise of them that sing do I hear. They were feasting and dancing around the idol. Joshua's loyalty at the mount is one of the main reasons the Lord chose him to succeed Moses.
- As soon as he came nigh unto the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger waxed hot, and he cast the tables out of his hands and brake them beneath the mount.
- He took the calf which they had made, burnt it in the fire, ground it to powder, strawed it upon the water, and made the children of Israel drink of it. Our forefathers were no joke about the law; Nehemiah likewise put hands on those who profaned the sabbath in his day.

**[Exodus 32:21-24](/bible/exodus/32#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/exodus/32#v21)</sup> And Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought so great a sin upon them?
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/exodus/32#v22)</sup> And Aaron said, Let not the anger of my lord wax hot: thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/exodus/32#v23)</sup> For they said unto me, Make us gods, which shall go before us: for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/exodus/32#v24)</sup> And I said unto them, Whosoever hath any gold, let them break it off. So they gave it me: then I cast it into the fire, and there came out this calf.

- Moses said unto Aaron, What did this people unto thee, that thou hast brought so great a sin upon them? He had left Aaron in charge, and came back to a camp deep in wickedness.
- Aaron answered, Let not the anger of my lord wax hot: thou knowest the people, that they are set on mischief; they said make us gods, I cast the gold into the fire, and there came out this calf. A leader cannot blame the congregation, the same excuse Saul gave; the charge has to be carried.
- The psalm gives the depth of it: they soon forgat his works and waited not for his counsel, they made a calf in Horeb and changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass, and they forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.

  Precepts:
  - **[Psalms 106:13-16](/bible/psalms/106#v13)**
    > <sup>[13](/bible/psalms/106#v13)</sup> They soon forgat his works; they waited not for his counsel:
    >
    > <sup>[14](/bible/psalms/106#v14)</sup> But lusted exceedingly in the wilderness, and tempted God in the desert.
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/psalms/106#v15)</sup> And he gave them their request; but sent leanness into their soul.
    >
    > <sup>[16](/bible/psalms/106#v16)</sup> They envied Moses also in the camp, and Aaron the saint of the Lord.

    They soon forgat his works and waited not for his counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness, and tempted God in the desert.
  - **[Psalms 106:19-23](/bible/psalms/106#v19)**
    > <sup>[19](/bible/psalms/106#v19)</sup> They made a calf in Horeb, and worshipped the molten image.
    >
    > <sup>[20](/bible/psalms/106#v20)</sup> Thus they changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eateth grass.
    >
    > <sup>[21](/bible/psalms/106#v21)</sup> They forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt;
    >
    > <sup>[22](/bible/psalms/106#v22)</sup> Wondrous works in the land of Ham, and terrible things by the Red sea.
    >
    > <sup>[23](/bible/psalms/106#v23)</sup> Therefore he said that he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them.

    They made a calf in Horeb and forgat God their saviour; he said he would destroy them, had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach, to turn away his wrath.

**[Exodus 32:25-29](/bible/exodus/32#v25)**

> <sup>[25](/bible/exodus/32#v25)</sup> And when Moses saw that the people were naked; (for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies:)
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/exodus/32#v26)</sup> Then Moses stood in the gate of the camp, and said, Who is on the Lord’s side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/exodus/32#v27)</sup> And he said unto them, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Put every man his sword by his side, and go in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and slay every man his brother, and every man his companion, and every man his neighbour.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/exodus/32#v28)</sup> And the children of Levi did according to the word of Moses: and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/exodus/32#v29)</sup> For Moses had said, Consecrate yourselves to day to the Lord, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother; that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.

- The people were naked, for Aaron had made them naked unto their shame among their enemies. That is the same nakedness of [Genesis 3](/bible/genesis/3), the shame of sin uncovered.
- Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, Who is on the LORD's side? let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him.
- Every man put his sword by his side and went in and out from gate to gate throughout the camp, and there fell of the people that day about three thousand men. The Lord chose those particular ones to die; that spirit would have wrecked the nation down the road, so he moved it out of the congregation. Do not be broken when someone leaves the truth; the Lord moves spiritually.
- Consecrate yourselves to day to the LORD, even every man upon his son, and upon his brother, that he may bestow upon you a blessing this day.

**[Exodus 32:30-35](/bible/exodus/32#v30)**

> <sup>[30](/bible/exodus/32#v30)</sup> And it came to pass on the morrow, that Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin: and now I will go up unto the Lord; peradventure I shall make an atonement for your sin.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/exodus/32#v31)</sup> And Moses returned unto the Lord, and said, Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made them gods of gold.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/exodus/32#v32)</sup> Yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin—; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/exodus/32#v33)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/exodus/32#v34)</sup> Therefore now go, lead the people unto the place of which I have spoken unto thee: behold, mine Angel shall go before thee: nevertheless in the day when I visit I will visit their sin upon them.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/exodus/32#v35)</sup> And the Lord plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.

- Moses said unto the people, Ye have sinned a great sin. They had broken the first two commandments just given at Sinai: no other gods before him, and no graven image to bow down to and serve.
- Moses returned unto the LORD to mediate: yet now, if thou wilt forgive their sin; and if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written. That is a real leader, putting himself in the way of harm for his people.
- The Lord answered, Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book; therefore now go, lead the people, and mine Angel shall go before thee; nevertheless in the day when I visit I will visit their sin upon them. And the LORD plagued the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 20:1-5](/bible/exodus/20#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/exodus/20#v1)</sup> And God spake all these words, saying,
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/exodus/20#v2)</sup> I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/exodus/20#v3)</sup> Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/exodus/20#v4)</sup> Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:
    >
    > <sup>[5](/bible/exodus/20#v5)</sup> Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me;

    I am the LORD thy God; thou shalt have no other gods before me, nor make any graven image, nor bow down to them, for the iniquity of the fathers is visited upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate him; the calf broke these first commandments.
